_comment: Design §4.4 authority baseline: sources in authority order, every routing-relevant domain listed here (no domain may fall back to registration order - that degeneration is what made two macro legs' auto order a coincidence of file collection order). Domain identifiers must exist in opendata/data/domains.yaml (cross-checked by tests). Domestic domains: ths is authoritative, akshare the fallback. fund_etf_daily is the one reversed domestic pair: the ths leg answers only a rolling 1827 days (measured, docs/evidence/C20), so it cannot answer 'since inception' and akshare stays first. Macro domains are listed per measured substitutability: a row orders only the legs sharing one (period, market), because source='auto' refuses to pick across markets (registry._reject_cross_market_auto). economy_unemployment puts oecd before imf on the measured publication shape: with the window end pushed to 2031, imf returns 6 rows dated after the last completed year 2025 (WEO projections mixed into the same value field) while oecd returns none (docs/evidence/C22). Measured there too: the two legs agree for USA (0.097pp) and JPN (0.174pp) but not for DEU (0.421pp over the 0.3pp tolerance), so they are not value-swappable for every area - open finding, not a ranking question. economy_cpi keeps ecb first on a declared, not measured, basis: the 1M legs are not value-comparable (euro-area aggregate vs a UK series on the eu-labelled leg, means 2.394 and 0.223, max per-date gap 10.181), so no value-level judge exists and the euro-area publisher wins. economy_gdp and economy_rate have one verified leg per (period, market) - listed so the coverage guard in tests/test_macro_routing.py cannot silently regress. Loaded by opendata/data/registry.py.
